title: U.S. House · Michigan's 9th District
area: Michigan's 'Thumb' region and northern Macomb County, including Romeo, Rochester and St. Clair, Sanilac and Lapeer counties.

context.text: Incumbent Lisa McClain (R) advanced unopposed from the Republican primary. Ray Pooley (D) won the Democratic primary.

candidates.name: Lisa McClain
candidates.currentRole: U.S. Representative (since 2021); House Republican Conference Chair

summary.text: Lisa McClain is the Republican incumbent, seeking a fourth term and serving as chair of the House Republican Conference. A Michigan business owner and nonprofit founder before Congress, she was first elected in 2020 and moved into party leadership in 2023. According to her official biography, she works on issues including agriculture, financial services, national defense, immigration, health care and veterans affairs.

background.text: Born April 7, 1966, in Stockbridge, Michigan, where she was raised and graduated from high school in 1984, according to Wikipedia.
Attended Lansing Community College and earned a bachelor's degree in business administration from Northwood University.
According to her official biography, spent more than 30 years building and growing a business before entering Congress. She also founded and served as president of North End Support Team.

Won the 2020 Republican primary for Michigan's open 10th District over Shane Hernandez and Doug Slocum, then defeated Kimberly Bizon (D) in the general election; the district was renumbered the 9th after redistricting, and she won re-election in 2022 and 2024.
Serves on the House Financial Services Committee and the Education and Workforce Committee, according to her official biography.
Served as Secretary of the House Republican Conference in the 118th Congress and was elected chair of the Conference for the 119th Congress.
Lives in Romeo, Michigan, with her husband, Mike, and their four children, according to her official biography.

priorities.text: Our economic system of capitalism provides the most significant opportunity for all Americans. It has proven time and again that it can raise all by incentivizing businesses to create jobs, raise wages, and provide competitive benefits that create more prosperity for the American worker and their families.
I will continue to push my colleagues in Congress to support a robust military that is the premier fighting force in the world. We can achieve peace through strength.
Life begins at conception, and I will always protect the sanctity of Life.

positions.summary: Says life begins at conception and she will always protect the sanctity of life; reintroduced a resolution supporting the Supreme Court's Dobbs v. Jackson Women's Health Organization decision and issued a statement supporting House passage of the Born-Alive Abortion Survivors Protection Act.
positions.quote: Life begins at conception, and I will always protect the sanctity of Life.

positions.summary: On energy policy, says she does not believe government should direct clean-energy investment through research and development grants, favoring private-sector-led development alongside continued oil, natural gas and pipeline production such as completing the Keystone XL pipeline.
positions.quote: I do not believe it is the government’s job to pick winners and losers when it comes to energy research and development grants.

positions.summary: Issued a statement praising House passage of the SAVE Act, which the release describes as requiring proof of citizenship for voter registration.
positions.quote: Rep. Chip Roy’s bill, the SAVE Act, protects the vote of every American—including women.

positions.summary: Issued a statement praising House passage of the Protection of Women and Girls in Sports Act, which bars transgender athletes from women's school sports teams.
positions.quote: The fact Congress had to enact legislation to keep men out of young girls’ locker rooms is insane.

record.text: Assigned to the Committee on Financial Services and the Committee on Education and the Workforce for the 119th Congress (2025-2026).
Chaired the Health Care and Financial Services subcommittee of the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform in the 118th Congress (2023-2024).
Elected chair of the House Republican Conference for the 119th Congress, defeating Kat Cammack 146-67 in the November 13, 2024 leadership election.
Reintroduced a resolution supporting the U.S. Supreme Court's Dobbs v. Jackson Women's Health Organization decision, January 20, 2023.

candidates.researchNotes: No 2026 campaign statements or Candidate Connection survey responses were found describing McClain's current policy positions beyond her committee record; positions above are drawn from her official House website's Life and Energy issue pages.

summary.text: Ray Pooley is the Democratic nominee, a CNC machinist and programmer making his first run for Congress. He describes himself as a third-generation manufacturer. His campaign website lists manufacturing jobs, family farms and tax fairness among its priorities.

background.text: Works as a CNC machinist and programmer. In his Ballotpedia survey he describes himself as a third-generation manufacturer with 15 years of personal experience in the industry.
Advanced from the August 4, 2026 Democratic primary for Michigan's 9th District; this is his first run for Congress.

priorities.text: Bringing manufacturing back to the U.S. and protecting the right to unionize.
priorities.quote: We will unleash American ingenuity to bring jobs home... We will ensure these new jobs pay a living wage by protecting the right to organize and join a union.

priorities.text: Supporting family farms against large agribusiness.
priorities.quote: It's time to break the grip of global conglomerates on our food supply. We will empower family farmers with the tools and knowledge for healthy soil, regenerative practices...

priorities.text: Medicare for All and expanded childcare services.
priorities.quote: I will fight to break the corporate monopolies on healthcare to ensure every American has the freedom to access quality, affordable care... through Medicare For All.

positions.quote: ...providing the security and peace of mind you deserve through Medicare For All.

positions.summary: Supports providing childcare services for all families.
positions.quote: ...we have the means and capability to provide childcare services for all, and therefore the responsibility to do so.

positions.summary: Supports raising the minimum wage alongside a cap on the ratio between CEO and worker pay.
positions.quote: ...raising the minimum wage while putting a maximum ratio for CEO pay...

positions.summary: Supports simplifying the tax code so that higher earners pay more and closing corporate tax loopholes.
positions.quote: That means simplifying the tax code so the ultra-wealthy pay their fair share, allowing us to cut taxes for working families, as well as closing all the tax loopholes these corporations take advantage of.

positions.summary: Supports domestic solar and wind power development over reliance on foreign oil.
positions.quote: By harnessing American-made solar, wind, and other innovative technologies, we can produce abundant, cheap, and clean power right here at home.

positions.summary: Opposes what he calls 'un-American ICE raids' while supporting a secure border and a faster legal immigration process.
positions.quote: End un-American ICE raids and enforce smart border policy, targeting root cause.

candidates.name: Destiny Clayton

summary.text: Destiny Clayton is the Green Party candidate for Michigan's 9th District. Little biographical information is available in public sources.

background.text: Advanced from the Green Party convention on April 25, 2026, and is on the November 3 general-election ballot.

candidates.researchNotes: No campaign website or public statements found; BallotReady lists only a Facebook page and military and digital-creator background.

candidates.name: Kevin Vayko

summary.text: Kevin Vayko is the Libertarian Party candidate for Michigan's 9th District and an environmental engineer. He also ran in the district's 2024 general election.

background.text: Born in Michigan and graduated from Almont High School.
Earned a bachelor's degree from Michigan Technological University in 2011 and works as an environmental engineer.
Was the Libertarian candidate in the 2024 general election for this district, which Rep. Lisa McClain won; advanced from the Libertarian convention on June 28, 2026.

candidates.researchNotes: No campaign website found; Ballotpedia shows no completed Candidate Connection survey and BallotReady lists only a LinkedIn page.

background.text: Advanced from the U.S. Taxpayers Party convention on July 18, 2026, and is on the November 3 general-election ballot.

candidates.name: Jim Walkowicz

summary.text: Jim Walkowicz is the Working Class Party candidate for Michigan's 9th District. He has appeared on this district's general-election ballot in earlier cycles.

background.text: Appeared on the general-election ballot for this district in 2022 and 2024, losing to Rep. Lisa McClain both times.
Advanced from the Working Class Party convention on June 6, 2026.

priorities.text: In a 2022 Michigan Public interview (his prior run for this seat): the economy, good jobs and a healthy environment.
priorities.quote: the economy and good jobs and healthy lifestyle. A healthy environment.

priorities.text: In a 2022 Michigan Public interview: affordable housing, good schools, safe environments and a working public health system.
priorities.quote: Affordable housing, good schools, safe environments. You know, a public health system that actually works.

positions.summary: In a 2022 Michigan Public interview, he said Congress should pass laws guaranteeing a right to control one's own body without government interference.
positions.quote: I think Congress needs to pass laws that guarantee a right for a woman to control her own body without government interference.

positions.summary: In a 2022 Michigan Public interview, he said he is against assault weapons but that banning them is not a simple answer without addressing underlying causes.
positions.quote: I'm absolutely against assault weapons. That's just crazy. But I think it's not as simple as saying ban them, because I think you have to look at the bigger issue.

candidates.researchNotes: No 2026 campaign website or 2026 interviews found. Statements come from an October 2022 Michigan Public interview from his prior run for this seat; he may have updated his views since.

statements.quote: I think we have to look at a cleaner, greener economy.
